rel stylesheet declares the stylesheet link relationship; other options are CSS property names, not that link type.

Shared external stylesheets enable synchronized styling; CSS does not itself supply domains, accounts or the document's semantic content.
HTML structures content; CSS styles it. They are distinct languages, not interchangeable names or networking control languages.
color and border are two declarations; border's multiple shorthand components do not count as separate source declarations.

font-weight sets glyph weight, not line height, text indentation or background color. Normal/bold are valid examples, not exhaustive values.
text-align:center centers inline text within its block; justify/right/left request distinct alignments. It does not promise to center the block itself.
line-height controls line-box height. Refine stem away from an unconditional baseline-distance definition, which varies with mixed inline content.
underline supplies an underlining decoration; overline and line-through draw elsewhere and initial does not inherently request underline.
text-indent controls first-line indentation in the ordinary textbook paragraph case; not weight, image width or table row count.
sans-serif is the generic fallback font family, not a border style, image format or color code.

H is hue angle on the color wheel; saturation/lightness are S/L and alpha is transparency.
Whitespace is the descendant combinator, including deeper descendants; it does not reverse ancestry or select prior siblings.
> selects direct-child F of E; parent or preceding sibling alternatives reverse the specified relation.
+ selects the immediately following element sibling sharing the parent; not descendants/parents. Non-element whitespace does not invalidate the relation.
~ selects later element siblings with the same parent, without requiring adjacency; preceding siblings/parents/root are not selected.
border-color changes the border color, while background-color changes the background and weight/indent control text. Border visibility also depends on its style, not claimed here.
strong is nested inside p, not a direct child of div; div > strong matches none in the snippet. Default color and head-only restrictions are irrelevant/false.
